problem: It says complete graphs 'use special conventions' for κ(G) ≤ λ(G) ≤ δ(G). With the chapter's own definition (removal disconnects G or leaves one vertex), K_n gives κ = λ = δ = n − 1, so the inequality holds for complete graphs with no extra convention. A student may wrongly conclude the inequality fails for K_n.
fix: Keep the caveat for the single-vertex graph only and say it plainly: 'The inequality κ(G) ≤ λ(G) ≤ δ(G) needs a connected graph with at least two vertices. For K_n it holds with κ = λ = δ = n − 1; only the one-vertex graph needs a convention, usually κ = λ = δ = 0.'

problem: '2-edge-connected' is used in the question but never defined in the chapter, so an ESL reader has to guess its meaning before answering.
fix: Add the definition in the question: 'A connected graph is 2-edge-connected when λ(G) ≥ 2, that is, no single edge removal disconnects it. A connected graph has a bridge e. Can it be 2-edge-connected? Explain using λ(G).'
